_comment: Landed rows whose capacity is still outstanding, with the reason and what would close it.
WHY NOT sources/manual/MANIFEST.json `wanted`. That queue is for a page the fetcher is
REFUSED and a browser can read, and its README says so in as many words: 'Not a place to
put anything a fetch failed on.' Only one entry here is that. The rest are the opposite
problem and a worse one -- the page is readable and the company has never stated a figure.
Filing those as retrieval jobs would send somebody to fetch a page that will not answer,
and would quietly convert 'nobody has said' into 'nobody has fetched'.
WHY NOT sources/batteries_candidates.json. That file is the admitted set waiting to LAND.
These rows have landed; what is missing is one field on a row that is already published.
`closes_it` is the test, not a guess: what a source would have to say for the row to be
filled. Printed on every build by report_candidate_gaps.py so the count recomputes itself
rather than rotting in a paragraph -- which is the lesson the batteries docket already
learned about carrying a shortfall as prose.

outstanding.reason: A REFUSAL, and the only one here. eng.sk-on.com serves a certificate for a different host and cannot be read by the pipeline; skonhungary.com answers 200 and states no capacity anywhere. The Hungarian government's Ivancsa announcement mentions Komarom only to say it already operates.
outstanding.closes_it: An SK On page stating a GWh figure for Komarom. Worth a manual retrieval, and the only entry here that is.

outstanding.reason: Samsung SDI's own Global Network locations page answers 200 and states no GWh for God. The 40 GWh figure in circulation is trade press (electrive, Battery-News) and is not admissible under the source rules for this pass.
outstanding.closes_it: A Samsung SDI page, filing or sustainability report stating a GWh figure for the Hungarian site.

outstanding.reason: Sunwoda's own release about the Hungarian factory answers 200 and states no GWh. The Hungarian government's announcement is in forints -- 580 billion, with a first phase of 93 billion.
outstanding.closes_it: A Sunwoda page or filing stating a GWh figure for Nyiregyhaza.

outstanding.reason: SVOLT's own announcement of the Lauchhammer factory, read from the Internet Archive, states no capacity. The row already recorded that when it landed, and re-fetching the capture confirms it.
outstanding.closes_it: An SVOLT statement giving a GWh figure for Lauchhammer. The company withdrew from the site in May 2024, so one may never exist.

outstanding.reason: Both sources on the row are German trade press. No Farasis statement giving a capacity for Bitterfeld-Wolfen has been read, and the row's own note already turns on the company's words being the only thing that moves it.
outstanding.closes_it: A Farasis statement giving a GWh figure for Bitterfeld-Wolfen.

outstanding.reason: THE COMPANY STATES THE ABSENCE. Tesla's own quarterly update prints a dash in the capacity column for 'Berlin 4680 - Construction' where Texas reads '>40 GWh Production'. Trade press carries 8 GWh rising to 18 GWh; under the standing press ruling the project's own sources decide, and they decline to give one.
outstanding.closes_it: A Tesla filing or update printing a capacity for Berlin 4680 rather than a dash.

outstanding.reason: Both 10-Ks were fetched and read in full this turn. Neither contains the string 'GWh' at all: Giga Arctic is described as 'a 120,000 square meter gigafactory', which is floor area and not capacity.
outstanding.closes_it: A FREYR or T1 Energy filing stating a GWh figure for Giga Arctic. The European business is now presented as discontinued operations and the site is being rezoned for a data centre, so one is unlikely.
